grammarChart.title: Passive Voice: Be + Past Participle
grammarChart.purpose: To emphasize the action or the receiver of the action, rather than the doer.

forms.example: The book is written by her.
The house was built last year.
The cake is being baked now.
The report was being prepared when I arrived.
The problem had been solved before the meeting.
The results will be announced tomorrow.
The work must be finished by Friday.

explanation: The passive voice is used when we want to focus on the action itself or the object that receives the action, rather than the person or thing performing the action (the agent). In English, the passive voice is formed using a form of the verb 'to be' (am, is, are, was, were, been, being) followed by the past participle of the main verb (the V3 form).  For example, in the active sentence 'The chef prepares the meal,' the focus is on 'the chef.' In the passive sentence 'The meal is prepared by the chef,' the focus shifts to 'the meal.' The agent ('by the chef') can often be omitted if it is unknown, unimportant, or obvious.
keyRules: Identify the object of the active sentence; it becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
Use the appropriate tense of the verb 'to be' that matches the original active sentence's tense.
Add the past participle (V3) of the main verb.
If the agent (the doer of the action) is important, it can be introduced with the preposition 'by'.
The passive voice is particularly useful in formal writing, scientific reports, news articles, and when the agent is unknown or irrelevant.
azarNotes: Think of 'be' as a 'helper' verb that changes its form to show the tense, and the past participle as the 'main action' word that stays the same regardless of tense.  For example, 'write' becomes 'written' in all passive forms: 'is written,' 'was written,' 'has been written.'  Remember the irregular past participles!

examples.passive: The assignment was completed by the students.
Research is being conducted by scientists.

examples.active: The company will launch a new product next month.
examples.passive: A new product will be launched by the company next month.

examples.active: The government has implemented new policies.
examples.passive: New policies have been implemented by the government.

commonMistakes: Using the base form or -ing form instead of the past participle (e.g., 'The book is write' instead of 'The book is written').
Incorrectly forming the 'be' verb for the tense (e.g., 'The report were finished' instead of 'The report was finished').
Overusing the passive voice, making the writing sound unnatural or indirect.
Forgetting to include 'be' when forming the passive (e.g., 'The cake baked by my mother' instead of 'The cake was baked by my mother').
ieltsTip: In IELTS Writing Task 2, the passive voice is very useful for discussing general issues, societal problems, or when you want to sound more objective and formal. For example, instead of saying 'I think people should recycle more,' you can say 'Recycling should be encouraged.' This sounds more academic and less personal.  However, don't overuse it; a balance with the active voice makes your writing more engaging.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form: The famous novel _______ by a renowned author.
Transform the active sentence into passive: 'The chef prepared a delicious meal.'
options: A delicious meal prepared by the chef.
A delicious meal was preparing by the chef.
A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.
A delicious meal is prepared by the chef.
quiz.answer: A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form: The report _______ by the committee tomorrow.
Identify the tense in the passive sentence: 'The results have been announced.'
Transform the active sentence into passive: 'The students are completing the project.'
options: The project is completed by the students.
The project is being completed by the students.
The project was being completed by the students.
The project has been completed by the students.
quiz.answer: The project is being completed by the students.
